name: Kaymard Copperpinch
summary: In Orgrimmar, Kaymard Copperpinch brings Smokywood Pastures' Winter Veil trade to the Valley of Strength. Travelers find festive wares there and can help with holiday troubles.

sections.title: A Goblin's Winter Veil
sections.body: Each Feast of Winter Veil, Kaymard Copperpinch brings Smokywood Pastures to the Valley of Strength. Great-father Winter receives visitors nearby while Kaymard sells fine treats, festive wrapping paper, and other holiday goods. For a goblin, no grand festival is complete without a lively exchange of coin.

sections.title: Holiday Complications
sections.body: During the festival, Kaymard also handles troubles that threaten Smokywood Pastures. Holiday confections go missing, and Metzen the Reindeer disappears. Kaymard calls on Horde adventurers to solve these problems and keep Winter Veil running smoothly.

faq.answer: During the Feast of Winter Veil, Kaymard Copperpinch trades in Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength for Smokywood Pastures. He sells fine seasonal goods and asks passersby to help with holiday troubles.

Smokywood Pastures is a vendor consortium that supplies food, treats, and seasonal goods for the Feast of Winter Veil across Azeroth. It supplies both the Horde and the Alliance and turns a tidy profit.

faq.q: Where can I find Kaymard Copperpinch?
faq.answer: Kaymard Copperpinch trades in Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength, near the central festival display where Great-father Winter sits during the Feast of Winter Veil.

faq.q: Why does he ask adventurers for help during the holidays?
faq.answer: During Winter Veil, Smokywood Pastures faces troubles that include stolen holiday sweets and the kidnapping of Metzen, its prized reindeer. Kaymard hires willing adventurers to recover the stolen goods and Metzen, and protect the season's profits.

angles.text: For the Horde, Kaymard brings Winter Veil trade to Orgrimmar, where goblin enterprise joins the traditional winter celebrations.
As a cook, you can find seasonal recipes and specialty ingredients for traditional holiday treats through Kaymard and his Smokywood Pastures associates.
